chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from Abān ibn Taghlib, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

There is no believer except that his heart has two ears within it: an ear into which the slinking whisperer blows, and an ear into which the angel blows. So Allah supports the believer by the angel; thus that is His saying:
“And He supported them with a Spirit from Him.”

key_terms.أُذُنَانِ: two ears, symbolizing two inward channels of influence
key_terms.الْمَلَكُ: the angel, the divine messenger who strengthens and guides inwardly
key_terms.الْوَسْوَاسُ الْخَنَّاسُ: the slinking whisperer, Satanic insinuation that withdraws and returns
key_terms.بِرُوحٍ مِنْهُ: with a Spirit from Him, a Qur'anic expression of divine reinforcement
key_terms.قَلْبِهِ: his heart, the inner locus of perception and spiritual reception
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٍ: a believer, one who possesses iman and is receptive to divine support
key_terms.يُؤَيِّدُ: He supports or strengthens, referring to Allah’s aid for the believer

ai.seo_question: How does Allah support the believer against Satanic whispering according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that the believer is inwardly addressed by two influences: the whispering of al-waswas al-khannas and the support of the angel. It explains that Allah aids the believer through angelic reinforcement, linking this meaning to the Qur'anic phrase, “And He supported them with a Spirit from Him.”
